blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Trailer/container/yard assets lack sensing; detention, dwell and theft are discovered in invoices. Cold-chain excursions surface at claim time.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower — Agentic Process Automation, Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration, Decision Intelligence Systems, Intelligent Document Processing as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: Food safety (where cold chain) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Agents operated as one fleet: roles, queues, budgets and audit trails.
Decision paths that run in milliseconds, with policy checks and full logging.
Contracts, claims and invoices read end-to-end: extraction, validation and downstream action.
Dynamic route/load re-planning within policy when events hit (re-plan in minutes at network scale)
Delay, detention and document exceptions remediated automatically with escalation (exception queues cleared autonomously)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Food safety (where cold chain) and CSRD/ISSB logistics emissions. Scope 3 transport emissions with auditability. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
